pregame.matchup_read: Two 6-2 teams, both on W4, meet at Paycor for the AFC North lead. Cincinnati is home and laying 3.5 with a total of 49.5. Mostly cloudy, 43F, so conditions should not rewrite either plan.
storylines: Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are tied at 6-2, though the Bengals hold the better point differential at +65 to +36.
ESPN's primer frames it as a battle for the division, Aaron Rodgers against Joe Burrow on Sunday night.
Ben Baby reported the Bengals are confident heading into the matchup, per the headline.
Cleveland sits 5-4 on an L2 and Baltimore is 4-5 on an L4, so the winner here can start pulling clear.
watch_for: Ja'Marr Chase after his 10 rec, 155 yds, 1 TD in Madrid. How much attention Pittsburgh gives him shapes everything else.
Cincinnati's third down work. They went 6-10 against Atlanta and had zero turnovers.
The run game split. Chase Brown had 9 car, 57 yds and Samaje Perine 11 car, 43 yds last week.
pregame.the_call: Bengals cover the 3.5. Burrow was 24/29 for 271 and 3 TD last out, the offense is at 7.1 yards per play form, and Pittsburgh has not faced that version of Cincinnati this year.

postgame.what_decided_it: Cincinnati was efficient and clean in Madrid. 7.1 yards per play, 6 of 10 on third down, zero turnovers, 3 of 4 in the red zone. Atlanta ran well at 6.5 a carry but threw for only 162 and took 12 penalties for 88 yards.
standouts: Joe Burrow: 24/29, 271 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT. Nothing wasted.
Tee Higgins: 5 catches for only 32 yards but two touchdowns.
postgame.division_meaning: Pittsburgh sits 6-2 on a four game win streak, Cincinnati 5-2 in the table and winners of three, with the best differential in the division at +48. Cleveland 5-3, Baltimore 4-5 and losers of four.
postgame.the_take: The run game is the quiet part of this. 123 yards on 24 carries at 5.1 a pop meant Burrow never had to force anything. Do that against Pittsburgh and the North shifts.
